intent.subject: Sayed (C-02), crouched beside the silenced radio set, face held in dark three-quarter view.
intent.action: He quietly voices his fear to Shalabi that the enemy may be waiting for them.
intent.setting: Tina Plain marsh at night, with the halted company just off-frame after the radio silence order.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Begin on a tight, shadowed three-quarter close-up of Sayed at the dead radio, then hold a restrained two-shot with Shalabi just at frame edge.
direction.blocking: Sayed crouches low beside the silenced set, turns only his eyes toward nearby Shalabi while the halted company remains an unseen presence behind them.
direction.performance_note: Keep the fear contained—Sayed speaks almost without breath, searching Shalabi’s face for reassurance rather than panicking.
direction.pacing: Slow, suspended beats with a brief whispered line and no release afterward.
direction.tone_ref: Grounded nocturnal war realism: oppressive silence, mud, darkness, and the sense of danger waiting beyond the reeds.

wardrobe.additions: sergeant's rank: three khaki cloth chevrons on the upper sleeve, plain shoulder straps and plain collar
visible_details: Sand-khaki 1973 Egyptian commando cotton jacket, wet and mud-splashed across the lower front and rolled forearms
Bare head with short black hair; no helmet or headgear
Khaki canvas Soviet-pattern chest rig: only the upper plain straps, metal buckles and closed-flap magazine pouches catch minimal red/cool rim light
Three khaki cloth sergeant chevrons on the upper sleeve, subtly readable when his turned arm catches light
Plain khaki collar and plain shoulder straps
Wet, darkened trouser fabric and muddy knee area may appear at the low frame edge; no waterline above the knees
No modern equipment, body armor, flag patch, chest eagle badge, or sunglasses
wardrobe.notes: Match the prior insert: radio illumination is now off. Red-filtered spill and blue-black moon rim reveal damp fabric texture without making the uniform appear clean or dry; retain WEAR_MUD with soaked mud-and-brine staining above the knees and a wet splashed jacket.

makeup.skin_state: Sun-darkened weathered face damp with cold sweat and fine brine sheen; sparse dark marsh-mud flecks along jaw, cheeks and forehead, with moisture catching the dim red flashlight and blue-black starlight.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed receding short black hair, wet and lightly mud-specked at the temples; natural grey at temples and thick bushy black mustache remain clearly defined, slightly damp.
makeup.notes: Keep his broad round face, deep forehead lines, bushy eyebrows and signature mustache intact. Fatigue is conveyed by shadowed deep-set eyes and taut, contained expression; no blood, cuts or wounds.

hand_items: small hooded red-filtered flashlight, held low beside the radio
dressing: Thin broken white salt crust over black slick mud
shallow mid-shin brine sheen and small sky-reflecting puddle patches at the low frame edge
a few sparse dark marsh reeds swallowed into the blue-black background
subtle crouch-disturbed mud and wet boot impressions
set.set_state: PRP-0007 sits braced low on a raised fold of webbing above the brine with its faceplate switched off; PRP-0008 is a folded topographic map held under its lensatic compass beside the radio, both kept dry on the same raised support while Sayed holds the hooded red-filtered flashlight low to graze them and his face.
set.notes: PRP-0008 is the library compass-and-map set, not a flashlight; the red-filtered flashlight is a necessary unlisted period hand-item library gap. Keep the radio, compass, and map free of mud and water; no readable markings or text are visible on the map.

camera.light: A tiny hooded red-filtered flashlight, kept just below Sayed’s chest beside the switched-off PRP-0007 radio, gives a weak upward-side red graze to his cheek, mouth and muddy hands; sparse cold blue-black moon and starlight provide a faint rear three-quarter rim on hair, shoulder and wet marsh texture. Keep the surrounding reeds and halted company swallowed by darkness, with no visible artificial fill.
camera.exposure_note: Expose approximately 1.5–2 stops under a normal night-face exposure: Sayed’s near eye, mouth and speaking cheek remain barely but clearly readable in the red/cool mixed low key, while the far side of his face and background fall into deep blue-black shadow; retain soft 500T grain and protect the red flashlight from clipping.
camera.framing_note: MCU in 16:9 with Sayed’s three-quarter face, both eyes, mouth, radio edge and any gesturing hand held inside the middle 75% height for the 2.39:1 crop. Keep his eyeline angled toward off-screen Shalabi at frame edge; preserve an empty dark edge rather than showing Shalabi, and keep the lip-sync mouth continuously readable.

action.choreography: Sayed stays in a low, stable crouch beside the silenced radio, keeping his movements contained so the whispered warning carries the tension without disturbing the set.
action.movement: Minimal: a controlled breath, slight eye turn toward off-screen Shalabi, and a small tightening through the shoulders while maintaining the crouch.
beats: Hold low beside the dark radio.
Keep one hand braced near, not operating, the set.
Shift only his eyes toward off-screen Shalabi.
Whisper the warning with contained breath.
Freeze again, listening into the marsh silence.
action.safety_note: Maintain a stable crouch on slick mud; keep the radio braced clear of brine and mud as established in the preceding insert.

reasons: The intent names the subject (Sayed/C-02), his dramatic action, the Tina Plain marsh setting, night time of day, and an appropriately tense, hushed mood.
It preserves the scripted dramatic beat: after the radio is silenced, Sayed asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
It references the available character and location library IDs. The radio is correctly treated as a listed prop by descriptive asset name; no unsupported ID is required.
The framing detail and halted company context do not introduce a new historical fact and are compatible with the locked beat.

Coverage is specified and supports the intended intimate, concealed exchange: a shadowed three-quarter close-up establishes Sayed’s fear, followed by a restrained two-shot that includes Shalabi without breaking the hush.
Blocking matches the scene intent: Sayed remains crouched at the silenced radio, directs only his eyes toward Shalabi, and keeps the halted company off-frame as an implied presence.
The performance note gives Sayed a controlled, fearful whispered delivery and explicitly avoids panic, fitting a restrained grounded historical war drama.
Pacing is clearly defined as slow and suspended, with no emotional release after the whispered line, sustaining apprehension.
The tone reference is consistent with the Tina Plain night-marsh setting and the scene’s tense, hushed mood.

The required silenced radio from the preceding insert is described only as generic dressing while the formal props list is empty. PRP-0007 must be explicitly placed and carried forward as the now-dark radio set for continuity.
revise_instructions: Add PRP-0007 to the set props list and identify it as the raised, switched-off radio beside Sayed; retain its placement clear of brine and mud. The flashlight may remain placed dressing/practical unless Sayed handles it.

reasons: The lighting plan omits the locked red-filtered flashlight as a facial source and instead attributes facial readability solely to moon/starlight. The shot design requires both red-filtered flashlight and starlight, with the mouth readable for lip-sync.
revise_instructions: Revise the light and exposure notes to include the low hooded red-filtered flashlight as a restrained warm/red grazing practical on Sayed's lips, lower cheek, moustache edge and hands, while preserving the cool moon/starlight rim and overall dark exposure.

reasons: The shot includes concrete on-camera action: Sayed quietly voices danger to Shalabi and turns only his eyes toward him. Marking action as not applicable leaves the required performance beat unplanned.
revise_instructions: Set applies to true and specify restrained choreography: Sayed stays crouched by the dark radio, shifts only his eyes toward off-frame Shalabi, and whispers the warning with his mouth visible. State that no weapon handling occurs and that the halted company remains off-frame.

reasons: The locked cast contains only C-02, and the action/set keep Shalabi and the halted company off-frame. The camera light and framing notes nevertheless permit and call for a visible sliver/soft presence of Shalabi at frame edge, which would introduce an unlisted on-screen character without wardrobe or makeup coverage.
revise_instructions: Remove the visible Shalabi/frame-edge presence from the lighting and framing plan. Keep Sayed alone in frame, with his eyeline directed toward off-frame Shalabi; retain the readable mouth, dark three-quarter view, radio edge, and restrained red practical.

reasons: The lighting description says the red-filtered flashlight is 'held low,' while Set establishes it as placed low beside the radio. This creates an unresolved continuity/prop-handling conflict: a held flashlight would require an identified holder and, if Sayed holds it, a hand-prop/action acknowledgment.
revise_instructions: Match Set: specify that the hooded red-filtered flashlight is placed low beside the radio and aimed upward, producing the restrained red facial graze. Do not imply that Sayed or an unseen person is holding it.

reasons: C-02 is correctly dressed in period-appropriate Egyptian commando uniform and Soviet-pattern webbing, with bare head, no modern equipment, and a mud/brine wear state consistent with the marsh.
The sergeant insignia, plain collar, and plain shoulder straps conform to the specified 1973 rank system.
The visible-detail scope is appropriate for an MCU and preserves the shallow-marsh waterline rule.
Makeup supports the established wet, muddy, brine-exposed condition without adding injuries, gore, or modern styling.
The described low-key facial treatment preserves readable signature facial features and supports the contained fearful performance.

The radio placement breaks immediate continuity: the prior insert establishes PRP-0007 braced low against unseen soldier webbing and held clear of brine, while this setup newly places it resting on a mud-and-salt hummock. No intervening action establishes that it was moved.
The flashlight is correctly treated as an un-IDed hand item, and the marsh dressing otherwise respects the shallow-water location rule.
revise_instructions: Keep PRP-0007 braced low against Sayed's webbing, clear of brine and mud, matching the previous insert. Remove the claim that it has been placed on a hummock, unless a concrete on-screen action establishes Sayed setting it there before this held speaking moment.

reasons: The static MCU, 85mm portrait lens, night looks, 16:9 generation and 2.39:1 crop protection all match the locked design.
The exposure and lighting notes keep the scene genuinely dark while retaining a continuously readable mouth for lip-sync and maintaining Sayed's three-quarter facial view.
Keeping Shalabi off-screen correctly follows the locked cast limitation despite the conflicting Director coverage note.
The restrained crouch, eye shift, whispered warning, and return to listening directly serve the beat's tense, hushed intent without inventing combat events.
Action is minimal and physically plausible on slick marsh ground, while explicitly maintaining the radio clear of brine.

PRP-0008 is a locked beat prop but is neither placed nor identified in the set plan. Instead, the plan introduces an un-IDed hooded red-filtered flashlight as a hand_item, despite the locked prop list including PRP-0008.

Because the flashlight is visible enough to motivate the specified red facial graze and is used by Sayed, it must be reconciled with the locked prop inventory and listed as the appropriate library hand prop if PRP-0008 is that flashlight.
revise_instructions: Place and identify PRP-0008 in the set plan. If PRP-0008 is the hooded red-filtered flashlight, replace the un-IDed hand_item with PRP-0008 in hand_props and retain its described low, controlled position beside the switched-off radio. If it is another locked radio-related item, specify its plausible, visible-or-off-frame placement while keeping the flashlight’s library status correctly accounted for.
Retain PRP-0007 braced clear of brine and mud, the switched-off state, shallow mid-shin marsh conditions, and the static period-appropriate dressing.

reasons: Both locked beat props are placed: the silenced PRP-0007 radio is raised clear of brine and mud, and PRP-0008 is present beside it on the same dry support.
The unlisted but necessary hooded red-filtered flashlight is correctly declared as a hand_item rather than a library hand_prop, and it motivates the specified low red illumination.
The shallow brine, salt crust, mud, reeds, and crouch-disturbed ground are period-plausible and comply with the location rule that standing water remains below the knee.
The radio faceplate being switched off directly continues the prior insert, while the map is constrained to show no readable text.
